note: Adapted from Light & Wilson's (1936) original description, originally in English; the alate is unknown (in the original: Alate.—Unknown) and the worker is not described. The measurement table (pp. 478—479) is partly incomplete in the OCR, so only the legible items are listed. The type specimen is a typical soldier (type coll. No. 238). Figure numbers and distribution records have not been translated. Word-breaks at line ends in the original have been joined.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head black with a deep purple sheen to dark red mahogany; the anterior half of the nasus reddish; antennae and pronotum brown; the remaining nota pale brown; sternites and legs yellowish brown. Head large; the shape of the head and nasus as in fig. 6 of the original. Nasus short, thick at the base, slightly raised; dorsal outline concave, but less concave than in G. admirabilus and not wavy; mandibles spinous, with only a faint tooth scar remaining a little below the middle of the apex. Antennae 13-segmented, shorter than in G. admirabilus and slightly longer than head plus nasus; segment 3 very long, more than twice segment 2; segment 3 longer than segment 4; segments 5—13 nearly equal in length, about one seventh shorter than segment 3. Cuticle weakly sclerotised; abdomen slender, not humped as in G. admirabilus. Measurements (mm; typical soldier, type no. 238): head plus nasus length 1.95; head length (excluding the nasus) 1.33; nasus length 0.62; antennal segment 3 length 0.20; segment 4 length 0.14.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Differs from G. admirabilus in: the dorsal outline of the nasus less concave and not wavy; the antennae 13-segmented and shorter; the mandibles with only a faint tooth scar; the cuticle more weakly sclerotised and the abdomen slender, not humped.
